## Retrieve and check · First 12 minutes

At 350 K and z₁=0.5, use Psat₁=150 and Psat₂=60 kPa.

- **3 min, alone:** predict the phase at 80, 95 and 110 kPa.
- **5 min:** at 95 kPa, check z₁=(1−β)x₁+βy₁ using x₁=0.388889, y₁=0.614035, β=0.493506. Check both composition sums.
- **2 min:** each person opens [Lab 01](labs/#experiment) and saves a baseline.
- **2 min:** compare checks and summarize in Thai.

::: {.thai-summary}
แยกองค์ประกอบ x, y, z ออกจากสัดส่วนไอ β แล้วตรวจสมดุลมวล
:::

[Before class: 3-page reading](files/preclass-week-02.pdf) · 15–20 minutes

Bring the [Week 2 worksheet](files/week02-practice.pdf). Today: does a small fitting error establish trust?

## The 180-minute class

| Activity | Minutes |
|---|---:|
| Opening question and essential concepts | 30 |
| One hand calculation | 20 |
| One lab demonstration | 20 |
| Break | 10 |
| Student pair investigation | 70 |
| Discussion, exit ticket and feedback | 30 |

The opening 30 minutes include the 12-minute retrieval activity. Pair work stays 70 minutes. Final block: discussion 20, exit ticket 5, feedback 3, closing 2 minutes.

## Activity and its reference

$$\mu_i=\mu_i^\circ+RT\ln a_i,\qquad a_i=\gamma_i x_i$$

The activity is dimensionless; γ is its correction relative to an ideal liquid solution using the pure-liquid standard.

For x₁=0.4 and γ₁=1.25, a₁=0.50. Residual and excess reference comparisons are in the reading and appendix.

::: {.thai-summary}
activity ไม่มีหน่วย และ a ไม่ใช่ γ ต้องคูณด้วยองค์ประกอบ x
:::

## Properties → prediction → fitting

1. Verify the Antoine form, units and applicable temperature range.
2. Predict P and y from a chosen liquid model.
3. Infer activities from observations, then compare model fits.

$$\gamma_i=\frac{y_iP}{x_iP_i^{sat}(T)}$$

This inversion assumes ideal vapor and negligible Poynting correction. Convergence, consistency and prediction are separate checks.

::: {.thai-summary}
ตรวจรูปสมการ Antoine หน่วย และช่วงอุณหภูมิ ก่อนเชื่อค่าที่ fit ได้
:::

## A vapor-pressure error becomes an activity error

Synthetic point: P=100 kPa, x₁=0.4, y₁=0.6 and P₁ˢᵃᵗ=120 kPa.

$$\gamma_1=\frac{0.6(100)}{0.4(120)}=1.25$$

Using 150 kPa instead yields γ₁=1.00. The measured mixture data did not change; the inferred liquid behavior did.

**Pause:** calculate a₁ for each case before comparing answers.

::: {.thai-summary}
ข้อมูลสารผสมเดิม แต่ใส่ความดันไอผิด ก็ทำให้แปลผล γ ผิดได้
:::

## An independent check

Work alone first, then exchange checks using the worksheet.

1. Write the Antoine equation, temperature unit and pressure unit; evaluate one Psat.
2. Substitute one observed T, P, x, y point into γ=yP/(xPsat); show units cancelling.
3. Check x₁+x₂=1 and y₁+y₂=1. Compare the same observations and property convention.

::: {.thai-summary}
เขียนแทนค่าจริงหนึ่งจุด การบอกว่า “ได้ตรงกับ lab” ยังไม่แสดงวิธีตรวจ
:::

## One demonstration · 20 minutes

[Open the core lab](labs/vle-input.html#vi-experiment)

Load and validate the synthetic example in Lab 08. Inspect its Antoine form and units, then fit one-parameter Margules. Compare predicted P and y with one observed point, then inspect the residual pattern.

Each person repeats the baseline and saves it. Pause here to resolve setup problems before model comparison.

## Pair investigation · 70 minutes

- 10 min: each person loads and validates the same baseline.
- 25 min: change one input and calculate.
- 20 min: calculate γ individually, then exchange checks and roles.
- 15 min: prepare one plot or table and a short explanation.

In Lab 08, validate the supplied synthetic example and compare one-parameter Margules with NRTL at alpha=0.3 on the same observations. Report one residual pattern and verify one activity coefficient by hand.

## Discussion · 20 minutes

Does a small fitting error mean the data and model are trustworthy?

Compare one residual pattern and one numerical check. Distinguish a converged fit, a consistency diagnostic and prediction on excluded data.

::: {.thai-summary}
fit ได้ดี ไม่ได้ยืนยันว่าข้อมูลถูกหรือทำนายนอกข้อมูลได้ดี ต้องตรวจแยกกัน
:::
